label: Next Senate Majority Leader: Schumer Vs. Van Hollen
kicker: The Race For Senate Democratic Leader
title: Chuck Schumer Vs. Chris Van Hollen
why: Senate Democrats choose their leader in December. Chuck Schumer has led them since 2017. On November 12, Chris Van Hollen announced he is running against him. Here is how the two have voted:

groups.name: Blocking Arms Sales To Israel
groups.about: Six attempts to stop specific weapons sales. All failed.
groups.more: Congress can block a weapons sale to another country by passing a resolution against it. Senators forced votes on six of these, each covering a different sale to Israel. Every vote was on whether to pull the resolution out of committee, and every one failed, so none moved forward.

groups.name: The 2026 Defense Policy Bill
groups.about: Covers troop levels, weapons buying and military construction.
groups.more: This yearly bill sets policy for the military: how many troops, which aircraft, ships and missiles to buy, and construction on bases. The final version also covered military pay and health care. It sets spending limits but does not itself provide the money. The six votes were steps along the way, from starting debate to approving the final version.

groups.name: Overturning An IRS Reporting Rule For Crypto
groups.about: Cancels a rule making some crypto platforms report sales to the IRS.
groups.more: In December 2024 the IRS issued a rule requiring decentralized finance platforms to report their customers' digital asset sales. Congress can cancel a recent rule by passing a resolution. The Senate voted on two versions of that resolution, each with one vote to take it up and one to pass it.

groups.name: Permanently Banning Fentanyl-Related Drugs
groups.about: Permanently puts fentanyl-related substances in the strictest drug category.
groups.more: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances, as a class, in Schedule I, the strictest category of controlled drugs. Offenses carry the same penalties as other fentanyl analogues, including mandatory minimum prison terms. It also changes the rules for researchers who study these drugs.

groups.name: The Energy Permitting Bill
groups.about: Would change permit and review rules for energy projects and power lines.
groups.more: The Senate is using a House tax bill, the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act (H.R. 2347), to carry a much larger package called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. The package would set deadlines for federal permits and environmental reviews, set a 150-day limit for filing many lawsuits against them, and change rules for power lines, geothermal, hydropower, nuclear licensing and mining. The version a Senate committee posted on November 7 keeps the original tax bill as one section. That section would stop taxing most payouts won by survivors of sexual abuse. Two of these votes were on taking up the bill and one was on ending debate on the package. The Senate has not held a final vote on it.

groups.name: The College Sports Bill
groups.about: Covers name and image deals, agent fees, transfers and schools' TV rights.
groups.more: The Protect College Sports Act sets national rules for athletes' name, image and likeness deals, requires agents to register and caps their fees at 5 percent, and gives athletes one transfer without losing eligibility. It also lets schools and conferences pool and sell media rights, and makes the cap on sharing revenue with athletes permanent.

groups.name: The ROAD To Housing Act
groups.about: Covers dozens of housing changes, plus rules for community banks.
groups.more: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act has 59 sections that create or change federal housing programs. Among them: support for permitting new kinds of apartment buildings, lighter environmental review for some rural projects, rules for manufactured housing, and closer oversight of housing counseling groups. It also includes sections on community banks.

groups.name: Luke Lindberg For A Top Agriculture Job
groups.about: Nominee for the Agriculture Department's top trade post.
groups.more: Nominated to be Under Secretary of Agriculture for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs. One vote ended debate on the nomination and the other confirmed him, 78 to 17.

groups.name: The 2026 Government Funding Bill
groups.about: Funds the military, health, education, transportation, housing and more.
groups.more: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 combines 5 of the 12 yearly funding bills. It funds the military and the Labor, Health, Education, Transportation, Housing, Treasury and State departments for the rest of the 2026 budget year, and Homeland Security through February 13, 2026.

groups.name: The March 2025 Stopgap Funding Bill
groups.about: Advanced a bill keeping the government open through September 2025.
groups.more: A continuing resolution that funded the government for the rest of the 2025 budget year, mostly at 2024 levels, and avoided a shutdown on March 14, 2025. This was the vote to end debate on it, which needed 60 senators.

groups.name: Sean Duffy For Transportation Secretary
groups.about: Nominee to run the Department of Transportation.
groups.more: Nominated to be Secretary of Transportation. The Senate confirmed him 77 to 22.

groups.name: Cutting The Defense Budget By 10 Percent
groups.about: Would have moved the money to veterans' dental care. Failed, 10 to 88.
groups.more: An amendment to the defense policy bill. It would have cut the Pentagon budget by 10 percent and used the money to expand dental care for veterans. It failed, 10 to 88.

groups.name: Setting Aside A Hemp Change In A Funding Bill
groups.about: Set aside an attempt to drop a new definition of hemp from the bill.
groups.more: The bill that ended the government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025 also changed the legal definition of hemp. An amendment tried to take that change out. The Senate voted 76 to 24 to set the amendment aside, which kept the change in the bill.

groups.name: Changing Debt Limit Instructions In The Budget
groups.about: A proposed change to the 2025 budget plan. Failed, 5 to 94.
groups.more: An amendment to the 2025 budget plan that would have changed its instructions on the debt limit. It failed, 5 to 94.
